title: Finite-field bounded constructible stratified generation
statement: Let $A$ be a finite field and $X$ a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Use ordinary uncompleted derived categories of module sheaves over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal B_A(T)$ for the complexes whose cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval and is constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]: there is a finite constructible locally closed stratification on which each cohomology sheaf is pro-étale locally constant with finite-dimensional $A$-module values. Every $P\in\mathcal B_A(X)$ can be obtained, up to isomorphism, from zero and finitely many objects $g_*j_!L$ by finitely many shifts and distinguished-triangle extensions. Here $S\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{g}X$ ranges over factorizations of constructible locally closed strata as an open immersion into the scheme-theoretic closure followed by its closed immersion [det-sf-flat-model-generation], and $L$ is a locally constant sheaf with finite-dimensional $A$-values on $S$ [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. A distinguished-triangle extension means the middle object of a distinguished triangle whose first and third objects are already constructed; no infinite sums or direct summands are required.

proof.text: Represent a finite construction by a natural-number-indexed sequence with a finite used prefix, a zero first object, and an isomorphism from its last object to the input. Prove directly that this property is replete and closed under generators, all integer shifts, and middle-term extensions of distinguished triangles. For an extension, concatenate the two used prefixes. Insert the second prefix's zero first object using a shift by zero of the first zero object; translate every reference in the second prefix by the first prefix length plus one. Transport the extension triangle along the two endpoint isomorphisms and append its middle term. All translated references remain earlier entries. This defines an isomorphism-closed triangulated object property without retracts.

proof.text: Apply SheafOfModules.isFlat_constantFieldModule to the lifted field ULift A and the original small pro-etale site. The existing essentially-small sheafification instances supply its site hypotheses; specialize the locally-bijective instance explicitly to the module universe rather than asking typeclass search to invert a maximum of universe levels. Mathlib's ULift field instance supplies the field structure. Thus every ordinary constant-field module sheaf is flat. The proved constant-scalar encoding equivalences in ProEtaleConstantModuleConstructibility and ConstructibleCoefficientSerre convert the given constructibility predicate to the coefficient-universe predicate expected by the flat-model theorem, without changing its strata or its meaning.

proof.text: For a constructible sheaf F, apply clauses (1) and (2) of det-sf-flat-model-generation using this flatness. Obtain an ordered finite stratification and a filtration of F whose factors are exactly the canonical flatModelProEtaleExtension objects. The recorded stratum-range equality transports constructibility of each stratum to the range of its immersion. For a restriction L, its local constancy and finite stalks give finite constant models by the proved finiteLocal_iff encoding lemma and the finite-model local-constancy theorem. Restricting and then extending the constant scalar action identifies those models with the intrinsic localized constant module sheaves. A finite underlying module is finitely generated, so these are precisely generators allowed by the target.

proof.text: Map the filtration's zero first term into degree zero. Each short exact filtration step gives its distinguished singleTriangle by lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle. Induct over Fin (str.n + 1), using the finite-construction property from Step 1 and the generator membership from Step 3 for the third term. Transport the last term by the filtration endpoint isomorphism. This constructs F[0].

proof.text: Take the isomorphism closure of the constructible-sheaf predicate. The preceding step constructs its degree-zero objects, and the singleFunctors shift isomorphism constructs each such sheaf in degree q. Convert the given cohomological bounds a <= b into the standard IsGE a and IsLE b conditions. Apply lem-sfb-degreewise-bounded-devissage with the natural length (b-a+1).toNat and the constant family of isomorphism-closed constructibility predicates. Its hypotheses on zero objects, extensions and degree-q single objects are exactly Steps 1 and 4. This is the finite good-truncation induction of Stacks Tag 08J5, reused from the proved library declaration; it constructs P without any Tor-amplitude or etale-origin assumption.

proof.text: Unpack the finite used prefix obtained for P. Restrict its sequence to Fin (n+1); replace every natural-number reference by its Fin (n+1) counterpart, which exists because that reference is at most the preceding step index. Fin.succ and Fin.last preserve exactly the natural indices used in the construction. The zero first term, endpoint isomorphism, and three alternatives are therefore the displayed target. Zero-length constructions and empty schemes require no separate nonemptiness hypothesis.

The statement is unchanged and true: it is the field-coefficient case of Bhatt-Scholze Lemmas 6.3.3 and 6.3.9 (pp. 45-46; perfect values equal finite-dimensional values over a field). It also holds in the small cases: zero, acyclic, empty X, one stratum, one cohomology degree. Step 1 meets every hypothesis of lem-exc-constant-field-module-flat: the V-small skeleton, lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification, and the local-bijectivity leaf. Step 2 meets the hypotheses of det-sf-flat-model-generation clauses (1)-(2): finite ring, Noetherian X, pro-etale site with ordinary constant-ring modules. That node's tower proof shows the 'iterated extension' is a finite filtration with quotients a_{k!}L_k = g_*j_!L_k. Step 3 is lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle (Stacks 0152) in the abelian category Mod(A_X). Step 4 follows from the good-truncation cohomology formulas of def-kun-truncations. Step 5 is lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle (Stacks 08J5), with the third term H^q[-q] and a correctly set-up induction from q=a to b. I accept all six declared tool_uses as generic tools. No duplicate exists: lem-sfb-stratified-tor-interval-devissage, lem-per-noetherian-ctf-flat-model, lem-per-constructible-extension-finite-stage and det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc all state something different. There are no new nodes and no SGA citations. FIX, two repairs: (C1/C4) clause (1) of the flat-model node gives only locally closed strata, while the item requires constructible ones. Step 2 now says X is a Noetherian space, so they are constructible, and cites def-weil-constructible-subset (Stacks 005L); it is added to uses and proof_deps. (C4) Step 5 said shifts of distinguished triangles are distinguished 'by def-weil-triangulated-category', which that definition does not state.
